The term "LLMflation" refers to a 10x decrease in per-token cost per year over the past 3 years. For LLM of equivalent performance, the inference cost is decreasing by 10x every year.

## Specific Cost Metrics

The most striking example is the cost trajectory for GPT-3-quality models: When GPT-3 became publicly accessible in November 2021, it cost $60 per million tokens, while the cheapest model to achieve the same score in late 2024 was Llama 3.2 3B at $0.06 per million tokens. The cost of LLM inference has dropped by a factor of 1,000 in 3 years.

For higher-quality models, models with an MMLU score of 83 have seen price reductions of about a factor of 62 since GPT-4 came out in March 2023.

## What's Driving This

The rapidly declining cost of LLMs is opening up new use cases that weren't commercially viable just a few years ago.

## Important Note

While per-token costs are falling dramatically, usage is growing as AI features gain traction, meaning total inference spending grew 320% even as per-token costs dropped 280-fold.
